concepts.gloss: A verb that is not one of the limited auxiliary verbs; this is Cambridge's label for the remainder of the verb inventory.
A lexeme that has more than one inflectional form and therefore has a paradigm.
The complete set of inflectional forms associated with a variable lexeme.
A member of the primary part of a verb's inflectional paradigm; the section's lexical-verb table identifies preterite and present-tense forms, while auxiliaries also have negative primary forms.
One of the plain form, gerund-participle, or past participle forms in the lexical-verb paradigm; modal auxiliaries lack this set.
An additional primary inflectional form available to auxiliaries but not to lexical verbs.
A modal auxiliary whose paradigm lacks all secondary forms; some modal auxiliaries also lack a preterite form.

concepts.term: invariant present form of modal auxiliaries
concepts.gloss: The single present-tense form of a modal auxiliary, used with subjects of every person and number rather than taking a third-person-singular -s form.
The additional person-and-number distinctions displayed by be in its primary forms, compared with other verbs.

rules.statement: Auxiliaries have additional negative primary forms, whereas lexical verbs do not have corresponding negative inflectional forms.
rules.condition: When a verb lexeme is lexical rather than auxiliary, its primary verb form (including a preterite or present-tense form) cannot itself bear the auxiliary negative form -n't.
rules.violation: A negative -n't form is created by attaching -n't directly to a lexical verb form, such as a lexical preterite or third-person-singular present form.

rules.concept: absence of secondary forms in modal auxiliaries
rules.statement: Modal auxiliaries lack all secondary verb forms: the plain form, gerund-participle, and past participle.
rules.condition: When a modal auxiliary is required in a position selecting a secondary verb form—after infinitival to, in a gerund-participial construction, or after perfect have—the modal auxiliary has no form that can fill that position.
rules.violation: A modal auxiliary is used as though it had a plain form after infinitival to, a gerund-participle form with -ing, or a past participle after perfect have.

rules.concept: invariant present form of modal auxiliaries
rules.statement: A modal auxiliary has one present-tense form for subjects of every person and number; it does not take a third-person-singular -s form.
rules.condition: When a modal auxiliary is the finite verb in a present-tense clause, its form remains the same with first-, second-, and third-person singular and plural subjects.
rules.violation: A present-tense modal auxiliary is given a third-person-singular -s suffix.

conflicts.description: Conflict originally identified because Chapter 3 §1.1 states that modal auxiliaries use one present-tense form with all subjects and do not take a third-person-singular -s ending, while the original wording of AGR-002 generalized present-tense agreement to all verbs. Resolved by narrowing AGR-002 to present-tense non-modal verbs and adding the modal exception with examples and a Chapter 3 source.
conflicts.proposed_resolution: RESOLVED with explicit human approval on 2026-11-05: AGR-002 now excludes modal auxiliaries from present-tense subject-verb agreement and cites Chapter 3 §1.1, p. 75. The new MORPH-006 rule records the invariant modal form.
